    Calm and cozy

    Polar bear cave

    30 minBlankets, a table, a flashlight, stuffed animals

    Drape blankets over a table to make a den. Crawl in with flashlights and read bedtime stories to the stuffed animals before they hibernate.

    Tip for grown-upsLeave one side open so the cave never feels too closed in.

      Sled dash

      Sled through the snow with Pip

      Help Pip zoom over the little hills. Jump over snowmen and presents, duck under snowballs, and grab hot cocoa along the way.

      How to play

      1. Click Start.
      2. Press the Space bar or the Up arrow to jump. Hold the Down arrow to duck under snowballs. On a phone or tablet, use the Jump and Duck buttons.
      3. Grab hot cocoa for extra points. If you bump into something, the game ends. Try to beat your best score.

      Make a snowflake

      Make your own snowflake

      Cut paper right on the screen, just like real paper snowflakes.

      How to play

      1. Click and drag across the white paper on the green mat. Each drag cuts a piece out.
      2. Your snowflake appears on the right. Each cut repeats all the way around, like real folded paper.
      3. Like it? Click Save my snowflake. Want a new one? Click Start over.

      Build-a-snowman

      Dress up a snowman

      Make a snowman look any way you like.

      How to play

      1. Click the buttons to pick a hat, a face, a nose, a scarf and more.
      2. Click Surprise me for a random snowman, or New name for a silly name.
      3. Then build a real one outside, or a sock snowman if there's no snow.

      Extras
      Little things, big difference

      Small ways to make break easier

      Break is a big change for a lot of kids. A few small habits keep the fun parts fun.

      Keep a few anchors

      Wake-up, meals and bedtime at about the same times give the day a shape, even when everything else changes.

      Show the plan

      A picture schedule each morning answers "what's next?" before it gets asked fifty times.

      Give a heads-up

      Visitors, trips and new places are easier with a little warning: a photo, a story, or "in five minutes we'll go."

      Make a cozy corner

      A quiet spot with a blanket, headphones and a favorite book gives everyone a place to reset when the house gets loud.

      Count down to school

      Start a countdown about two weeks before school starts, so the first day back isn't a surprise.

      When is break?

      Most school districts near our centers let out December 18 to 21 and head back January 4 to 6. Look up your district's exact dates.

      When routines need a little more help

      Picture schedules and first-then boards are tools our therapists use every day. If changes, routines or communication are hard for your child most days, not just over break, ABA therapy may help.

      Treetop provides ABA therapy for children from 18 months to 18 years, at our centers and at home, and we work with most insurance plans.

      Good to know

      Anything else? Call us at (855) 800-9361.

      Ask away.
      Is the kit really free?

      Yes. Pop in your email and you'll get all 10 printables right away. We'll also send a few short emails over break with more ideas, and you can unsubscribe anytime.

      What ages is it for?

      Most of the kit works for toddlers through elementary school. The planner is for grown-ups. Use what fits your child and skip the rest.

      Do I need a printer?

      It helps, but you don't have to have one. You can show the sheets on a phone or tablet, or print them at a library or office store. If you do print, card stock or tape over the cards makes them last.

      Does my child need to be in ABA therapy to use it?

      Not at all. These printables work for any child who likes to know what's coming next. Lots of families use picture schedules and first-then boards at home.

      Can I share it with a friend or teacher?

      Please do. Send them the link to this page so they can grab their own copy.

      Who is Treetop?

      Treetop provides ABA therapy for children from 18 months to 18 years, at our centers and at home. We made this kit because break is a big change for a lot of kids, and a little planning goes a long way.
